config.notes: The orchestrator (your main session) runs on this tier. Opus 5.5 orchestrates well: it is capable, has no frontier allowance cap, and costs well under half the frontier tier's price. Keep security detail inside the security subagents: Opus 5.5 carries the safety classifier, and a flagged request in the main session moves the whole session to the fallback model until /model. Stored once so a single edit moves it. If moved to claude-fable-5-2: orchestration and peer-agent communication quality improves (the frontier tier's core strength), but the frontier tier draws down its allowance faster and is subject to plan caps, and the same main-session fallback applies. trigger_model is advice, not enforcement: nothing in the plugin can set the main session's model, so apply it yourself with /model (or the model setting) at session start.

task_tier_rules.rationale: Design and spec framing is where capability compounds; predictably code-heavy design should start on Opus 5.5 to avoid paying frontier drawdown on code-dense output.

A spec review is judged on catching design gaps before a builder runs, where the frontier tier's strength compounds; run it through the architect agent and keep the same reviewer across rounds. Security-heavy specs also go to reviewer-security.
Opus 5.5 matches the frontier tier closely on structured reasoning at half the cost and no allowance cap; escalate to Fable only when the problem is ambiguity-dominated.

task_tier_rules.surface_note: agent-definition full ID; pass no model
task_tier_rules.rationale: Hard constraint: run on reviewer-security, pinned by full ID, never on an alias that can move. A cyber-flagged request re-runs on Opus 4.8 by itself and the next ones return to Opus 5.5; keep fallback on automatic switching, because in 'ask each time' a flagged subagent fails instead. In the maintainer's own runs, 37 security reviews on Opus 5.5 or Fable 5.2 (about 2,000 turns) never fell back.

task_tier_rules.surface_note: agent-definition full ID; pass no model
task_tier_rules.rationale: Hard constraint: run on testing-red-team or testing-pentester, pinned by full ID, never on an alias that can move. On the classifier-carrying tiers (Fable models, Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Opus 5) nearly every offensive request would be flagged and run twice. Opus 4.8 is documented as the fallback target for cyber-flagged requests, not as a classifier source; it is active, with retirement not sooner than 2027-05-28.
With a full spec Sonnet delivers near-parity output at a fraction of the cost and parallelizes cleanly.
Roughly 3 or fewer tool calls with a specific question; any larger model is pure waste.
Sustained multi-subagent orchestration is a named frontier-tier strength that compounds over long sessions; keep security content out of its messages to avoid fallback swaps.
Navigating ambiguity is the frontier tier's headline strength and this work is mostly prose, so it rarely trips the cyber or bio classifier; low volume keeps allowance impact small.
Documentation from existing source material is structured transformation Sonnet does well; escalate to Opus 5.5 only for architecture-narrative docs needing real synthesis.

task_tier_rules.surface_note: agent-definition full ID; pass no model
task_tier_rules.rationale: Review compounds; Opus 5.5 gives near-frontier review quality at lower cost than Fable. Security-heavy review goes to reviewer-security instead; fast mode helps latency-sensitive gates.
Well-trodden patterns with clear acceptance criteria; Sonnet is the reliability floor (Haiku only for genuinely trivial single-file changes).

agent_defaults.rationale: Every task this agent runs is defensive security review, so its default IS the defensive security pin (claude-opus-5-5), by full ID in the agent definition, not the opus alias (an alias follows a same-family main session, an Opus 4.8 one included). A cyber-flagged request re-runs on Opus 4.8 automatically and later requests return to Opus 5.5. In the maintainer's own runs, 37 security reviews on Opus 5.5 or Fable 5.2 (about 2,000 turns) never fell back, and across 300+ reviewer runs on classifier-carrying models one fell back, automatically, for 15 turns, then returned to Opus 5.5.
Offensive-security engagement lead; permanently pinned to 4.8 including attack-narrative synthesis. Agent-definition full-ID surface only.
Pentest execution is dual-use content by definition; pinned to 4.8 via the agent-definition full-ID surface.
UI and component implementation against a spec is Sonnet's sweet spot; escalate gnarly state-management or accessibility-architecture problems to Opus.
API and service implementation given a spec fits Sonnet; escalate destructive schema/migration design decisions to Opus before execution.
Test authoring, coverage passes, and bug repro are mechanical and parallelizable; escalate flaky-test root-cause hunts to Opus.

Quality-gate verdicts compound; Opus 5.5 gives near-frontier review quality at lower frontier-allowance cost. Pinned by full ID, not the opus alias: an alias follows the parent session's model when the parent is the same family, so under an Opus 4.8 main session the alias would silently run this gate on 4.8.

A standards-citing quality gate is adversarial verification, not design authoring; Opus 5.5 matches the code-review tier and keeps the frontier allowance for the Designer. Pinned by full ID for the same-family reason given for reviewer-code.
System design, ADRs, spec review and trade-off framing are exactly where the frontier tier's ambiguity and spec-framing strength compounds; low task volume keeps drawdown acceptable.
Product and UX design - journeys, wireframes, interaction and visual design - is creative, ambiguity-heavy work where the frontier tier's strength compounds.

Requirements and epic breakdown from a stated goal is structured-reasoning prose work Sonnet handles reliably at a fraction of the cost; escalate genuinely ambiguous greenfield discovery to Fable, or to Opus 5.5 when a breakdown needs deep synthesis.
Docs and knowledge-base maintenance from existing material is structured transformation; Sonnet is the best token-to-quality tier for it.
Versioning, changelog collation, and release checklists are procedural but consequential; Sonnet is the reliability floor, Haiku acceptable for pure changelog collation sub-steps.

Lateral thinking and assumption-challenging is ambiguity work where the frontier tier is strongest. Runs once per spec and per significant design decision; its output is two or three short counterpoints, so volume and allowance cost stay small.

notes: Model surfaces and why aliases: a sub-agent definition's model: frontmatter accepts either an alias or a full model ID; the live Agent tool takes only aliases {fable, opus, sonnet, haiku}. Nine agents use the alias in frontmatter (architect, designer, loki: fable; developer-backend, developer-frontend, testing-qa, business-analyst, writer-technical, release-manager: sonnet), so each follows the current model of its tier and a new generation needs no edit to their files (default_model records what the alias resolves to today on the Anthropic API: fable = claude-fable-5-2, opus = claude-opus-5-5, sonnet = claude-sonnet-5-5, haiku = claude-haiku-5-5, checked 2026-11-26; in Claude apps gateway sessions fable is Fable 5 unless ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_FABLE_MODEL is set; Bedrock and Foundry resolve aliases to older models). Five agents keep an explicit full ID instead. The two offensive agents (testing-red-team, testing-pentester) stay on claude-opus-4-8, because an alias can move to a classifier-carrying tier and on those tiers nearly every offensive request would be flagged and run twice. The three reviewers (reviewer-code, reviewer-ux, reviewer-security) are pinned by full ID claude-opus-5-5, an exception to the alias rule, for a different reason: an alias follows the parent session's model when the parent is the same family (Claude Code subagent docs, 'Which version a model alias selects'), so under an Opus 4.8 main session `opus` would silently run the review gates on 4.8. The same exposure exists for any alias agent whose tier matches the main session: with a Fable main session the fable agents run on that session's Fable version, with a Sonnet main session the sonnet agents follow it; with the recommended Opus 5.5 main session neither occurs, but changing trigger_model changes what the alias agents run on.

Security enforcement is by ROUTING, not a per-agent override column. Hand defensive security review to reviewer-security (pinned to claude-opus-5-5) and offensive work (red team, pentest, exploit development) to testing-red-team or testing-pentester (pinned to claude-opus-4-8), all via full-ID frontmatter. A plugin agent's model is fixed by its definition unless the spawn passes a model. The order for a subagent is: (1) the per-invocation model parameter on the Agent call (aliases only), (2) the definition's model field, (3) CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL, (4) the parent's model; a mod's agent.spawn hook model beats (1), and CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL_FORCE=1 ignores (1) and (2). A model passed on the Agent call therefore replaces every pin, which is why hard rule 3 says to spawn roster agents with no model argument. Apart from a classifier fallback, an agent does not switch its own model mid-task, so there is no enforceable per-agent override; the routing decision is the control.

Frontier-tier allowance discipline: the frontier tier (Fable) draws down its allowance faster than Opus and is subject to plan caps (exact rates are plan-specific). Reserve it for tiers where its ambiguity/design/orchestration strength compounds (design/spec, long orchestration, brainstorm, architect, designer, loki). Do not route mechanical or logic-bound work to it.

Safety classifiers and fallback (Claude Code model-config and subagent docs, checked 2026-11-26): Fable models (5, 5.1, 5.2), Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5 and Opus 5 run safety classifiers that mostly flag cybersecurity and biology content. Fable models and Opus 5.5 re-run cyber-flagged requests on Opus 4.8 and bio-flagged ones on Opus 5; Opus 5 re-runs cyber on Opus 4.8 and refuses bio; Sonnet 5.5 re-runs cyber on Sonnet 5 and refuses bio. In a subagent, with fallback set to switch automatically, the flagged request re-runs on the fallback and the session's model is unchanged; with 'ask each time' the subagent fails ('Agent terminated early due to an API error'). In the main session a fallback stays until /model (checked 2026-10-08); switchModelsOnFlag=false makes the main session ask. Opus 4.8 is documented as the fallback target, not as a classifier source. Ordinary coding content is not a documented trigger; code-heavy tiers sit on Opus 5.5 or Sonnet for cost, not to dodge a swap.

trigger_model is stored once in config so the orchestrator tier is edited in one place. Whatever it is set to, keep security detail inside the security subagents so the orchestrator's own flag-prone message volume stays near zero: a flagged request in the main session moves the whole session to the fallback model until /model. It is advice only: nothing enforces it, and the main session's model is set with /model.
Fast mode (Opus, toggled with /fast) fits latency-sensitive quality gates (code review) and high-throughput reasoning passes.

Destructive schema/migration changes: the backend developer (developer-backend) must escalate the design decision to a capable tier and follow backup-first, manual-SQL, data-loss-warning policy before execution, regardless of its Sonnet default.

Pin by full ID only where the guarantee matters (the two offensive agents on claude-opus-4-8, the three reviewers on claude-opus-5-5); everywhere else the alias in frontmatter is intended, so the roster tracks the current model of each tier.
